validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE — CONFIRMED, high confidence, multiple independent origins. This is the 36-inch main Kurdistan Gas Pipeline carrying natural gas from the Summail gas field to the Duhok (Dohuk) Gas Power Station, first gas May 2014. Corroborated by: (1) KRG Ministry of Natural Resources primary press release 'First Gas Arrives at Duhok Power Station' (archive.gov.krd) — 'a 36-inch main Kurdistan Gas Pipeline was constructed from Summail to the Duhok Power Station, plus a feeder line from the gas field... power station located 40 kilometres from the field... initial ~55mmscf/d ramping to 120mmscf/d, eventually ~200mmscf/d'; (2) Oil & Gas Journal ('DNO to develop Summail gas field in Iraqi Kurdistan') — Summail is a GAS field, operated by DNO (40%) with Genel (40%) and KRG (20%) under the Dohuk PSC, supplying the Dohuk power plant; (3) Rudaw (independent Kurdish outlet) confirming gas from Summail to the Duhok power station at 120 MMcf/d long-term; (4) Mass Group Holding page for the Duhok Gas Power Station (the destination plant, ~1000 MW, GE Frame-9E turbines, dual gas/diesel, Gawasha on the Duhok-Zakho road). These are independent of GEM and of each other. CLASSIFICATION — correct: a gas transmission trunk to a power station, NOT an oil/NGL line (it is absent from the GulfPub Iraq oil roster) and not a plant-internal line. DUPLICATE — none: no other roster row runs Summail->Duhok; it is distinct from the Khor Mor-sourced KRG gas lines P6823 (Khormor-Pirdawood, Khor Mor->Erbil) and P6827 (Khormor-Jambur-Kirkuk). SPEC — length 40 km, diameter 36 in, capacity 120 MMcf/d, start 2014 all corroborated (see below). CAVEAT 1 (diameter): an early OGJ field-development article mentions a 24-in gathering/feeder pipeline into the regional gas network; the authoritative completion release + Genel + KAR Group statements all give 36 in for the MAIN Summail->Duhok line, so 36 in stands (the 24 in likely refers to the field feeder/gathering segment). CAVEAT 2 (length): 40 km is the sourced field-to-city distance ('power station located 40 kilometres from the field'), i.e. an approximate straight-line figure, not a surveyed pipe length. CAVEAT 3 (owner): GEM Owner='Kurdistan Government' is only single-sourced; the line was built by KAR Group (private KRG contractor) and the gas is produced by the DNO/Genel/KRG Dohuk PSC — consider KAR Group as operator on the operators/owners tab.

validity.recommendation: Change FuelSource 'Semel Field' -> 'Summail Gas Field' and fix the gem.wiki text 'Semel Oil Field' -> 'Summail Gas Field'. The source is a GAS field named Summail, not an oil field.
validity.researcher_notes: ATTRIBUTION ERROR. GEM records FuelSource='Semel Field' and the gem.wiki narrative calls the origin 'Semel Oil Field'. Both are wrong on two counts: (a) it is a GAS field, not an oil field — Oil & Gas Journal's headline and body ('DNO to develop Summail gas field'), the KRG MNR release ('gas from the gas field at Summail'), and Genel/DNO PSC reporting all describe a natural-gas field feeding a power station; and (b) the proper field name is 'Summail' (the Dohuk PSC's Summail gas field operated by DNO/Genel), whereas 'Semel' is the name of the surrounding district/town (Semel/Sumel), conflated into the field name and the pipeline title. The pipeline row and title can retain the familiar 'Semel-Duhok' label if desired, but the FuelSource cell should name the actual producing asset: 'Summail Gas Field'. This is a data-quality/attribution defect, not an existence problem.

routes.corridor_desc: The line runs roughly 40 km from the Summail gas field to the Duhok Gas Power Station, both within Duhok (Dohuk) governorate, Kurdistan Region of Iraq. The producing field lies in the Dohuk PSC block described as the southwest neighbourhood of Duhok (~80 km north of Mosul); the destination Mass Global power station sits at Gawasha on the Duhok-Zakho road northwest of Duhok city. Sources give only the ~40 km field-to-station distance, so the corridor is a loose ~40 km bound trending generally north/northwest from the field to the Gawasha plant. Precise field coordinates were NOT independently sourced (left null, not fabricated); the plant coordinate is an approximate placement of the Gawasha/Duhok-Zakho-road power station (~36.95N, 42.78E) and should be treated as approximate, not a surveyed endpoint.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from the KRG MNR release (start=Summail gas field, end=Duhok Power Station, 40 km apart) and the Mass Group Holding page for the Duhok Gas Power Station (destination plant at Gawasha, Duhok-Zakho road). No source gives a routed geometry or field coordinates, so the field endpoint lat/lon are left null and the plant endpoint is an approximate Gawasha-area coordinate; suggested accuracy 'low'. No coordinates were fabricated.

summary: P7457 Semel-Duhok is a REAL, independently confirmed 36-in gas line (Summail field -> Duhok/Gawasha power station, 40 km, 120 MMcf/d, 2014); one attribution concern: FuelSource 'Semel Oil Field' is wrong -> should be 'Summail Gas Field' (a gas, not oil, field).
